Excellent! The White king on g4 is checkmated by the rook on f4 – it cannot move to f5, f3, h4, h5, or h3 (all controlled by the rook or pawns).

**Coaching Note:**

When your opponent's king advances into the center, drive it forward relentlessly with checks. A king cut off from safety can be mated by your active pieces. Here, h4+ forces the king up the board, and Rb4+ keeps pushing—when White tries to create an escape square with f4, it's checkmate on f4. Always look for a forcing sequence that improves your piece activity, even when you're down material.
